shared_elements: frontal schematic anthropomorphic figure carved in low relief on a block/slab
head or face at top with brow/eye features rendered as paired hollows or arcs
shoulders wider than the tapering base
arms as curved ridges bent inward across the chest/torso, converging toward the middle
raised ridge along the vertical midline (nose/spine)
justification: Both depict a rigid, frontal, block-like anthropomorphic figure with a head at the top, wide shoulders, and curved arm-ridges bent inward to meet across the torso in very low relief, a fairly specific schematic convention. The main difference is that A carries additional distinct iconography — a large chest disc, belt/waist bands, and patterned incision on the head — while B shows only the bare facial hollows and limb ridges, with no discs, bands or ornament and a more ambiguous face-versus-body reading.
